subject: Literature
title: Langston Hughes and the Harlem Renaissance
description: Learn Langston Hughes and the Harlem Renaissance in one minute.

hook.text: Langston Hughes fused jazz and blues rhythms with poetry, creating a Black American voice literature had never heard.

buildup.text: His poem 'The Negro Speaks of Rivers' was written at eighteen on the back of an envelope crossing the Mississippi.

discovery.text: Hughes insisted that Black art should celebrate Black life, not imitate white literary standards.

twist.text: Some Black critics attacked him for using dialect and jazz forms, calling his work insufficiently dignified.

climax.text: Hughes proved that the music of everyday Black speech was the material of great poetry, not a limitation.

punchline.text: He turned the rhythms of Harlem into immortal verse.

quiz.question: What musical forms did Hughes incorporate into his poetry?
